title: Find and Delete Duplicate Files Safely with Python
description: Quickly scan your directories and purge duplicate files by checking their exact cryptographic hash. The included production kit adds chunked hashing for large files, size pre-filtering, and an essential dry-run mode.

beats.voice: Fourteen duplicate files gone, eighty megabytes back, zero manual clicking.
Scanning subfolders recursively gives you every file path without caring how deeply nested they are.
Hashing each file by its raw bytes spots exact duplicates even if someone changed the filename.
If the hash was already indexed, delete the clone on the spot and reclaim disk space.
Whole files load into memory here, so the kit adds streaming chunks and a dry run before seeing

kit_readme:
SETUP
1. Ensure Python 3.9 or higher is installed.
2. No third-party packages are required. The script relies entirely on standard library modules (pathlib, hashlib, argparse, logging).
3. Save tool.py into your project directory.

HOW IT WORKS
tool.py cleans up duplicate files in three stages:
1. Fast size grouping: It groups files by byte size. Files with unique sizes are never hashed, saving massive disk I/O.
2. Chunked cryptographic hashing: Files sharing identical sizes are hashed using SHA-256 in 64 KB memory chunks.
3. Safe duplicate resolution: The first file encountered is preserved as the original. Duplicate copies are recorded and deleted (or logged during dry-run).

Run a dry-run test first:
python tool.py --dir /path/to/folder --dry-run

Run live cleanup:
python tool.py --dir /path/to/folder

ADAPTING IT
- Moving instead of deleting: Replace `p.unlink()` with `p.rename(trash_folder / p.name)` to archive files instead of permanently removing them.
- Extension filtering: Add an extension check in the loop (e.g. `if p.suffix.lower() in {'.pdf', '.png'}:`) to target specific file formats.

LIMITATIONS
- Symbolic links and system shortcuts are skipped to prevent circular traversal.
- Identical files with different metadata (like modified date) will still be treated as duplicates because hashing inspects raw byte content.

SUPPORT
Provided as-is without warranty. Always run with `--dry-run` first to preview changes before deleting production assets.
